content: Starting local pi documentation review for TUI/session/server-extension constraints before external comparisons.

Read local pi README and docs for interactive mode, sessions/session-format, SDK, RPC, extensions, TUI components, themes, keybindings, settings, packages, Termux, terminal setup, tmux, and selected SDK/RPC/extension examples. Key implementation paths appear to be: full TUI via interactive mode/terminal, SDK/RPC custom UI via event stream, or direct session-file parsing/management.

observation: Pi is a minimal terminal coding harness with four modes: interactive TUI, print/JSON, RPC for process integration, and SDK for embedding. It explicitly supports extensions, skills, prompt templates, themes, and pi packages; mobile can either reuse interactive mode or build a custom SDK/RPC UI.

Pi TUI components are render(width)->string[] plus optional handleInput/invalidate; extensions can replace the editor, show overlays, widgets, custom footer/header/status, message/tool renderers, and custom components. Those APIs are terminal/ANSI-oriented and are the route to direct reuse of community TUI extensions.

Extensions have full TUI support only in interactive mode. In RPC mode, ctx.ui dialog/fire-and-forget methods work through JSON requests, but ctx.ui.custom returns undefined and TUI-specific methods such as setWorkingIndicator, setFooter, setHeader, setEditorComponent, setToolsExpanded are no-ops/degraded.

RPC mode exposes prompt/steer/follow_up/abort, model/thinking, session switch/fork/clone/state/messages/stats, bash, commands, and streamed agent/tool/message events over JSONL. It has an extension UI sub-protocol for select/confirm/input/editor/notify/status/widget/set_editor_text but explicitly cannot render arbitrary custom TUI components.

The SDK exposes createAgentSession and createAgentSessionRuntime. AgentSessionRuntime is the same layer used by interactive/print/RPC and supports replacing active sessions via newSession/switchSession/fork/import flows; after replacement, apps must re-subscribe and re-bind extensions.

Sessions are JSONL files under ~/.pi/agent/sessions organized by cwd. Entries form a tree via id/parentId, enabling /tree navigation, /fork, /clone, labels, compactions, branch summaries, custom extension entries, model/thinking changes, and display names.

Pi can run directly on Android through Termux with nodejs, git, termux-api, and npm install -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent; limitations include no image clipboard and Android/Termux storage/native dependency caveats.

@earendil-works/pi-tui has a Terminal interface, but InteractiveMode currently hardcodes new TUI(new ProcessTerminal()) in its constructor. Without an upstream change to inject a custom Terminal, the no-fork way to reuse the whole TUI remotely is to run pi inside a PTY and stream terminal bytes.

The included RPC client example demonstrates building a custom TUI over RPC and handling extension UI requests, but it necessarily reimplements display semantics and only supports the RPC-degraded extension UI surface.

content: Local pi documentation review complete. Proceeding to GitHub community search and specific project comparisons.
Searching GitHub/npm for community projects that mention or integrate @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent, pi packages, or pi mobile/client ideas, excluding the official pi-mono repository.

observation: InteractiveMode constructs `new TUI(new ProcessTerminal(), ...)` directly in its constructor, so the current public API does not let a mobile/web host inject a custom Terminal transport into the native TUI. Reusing the exact TUI without upstream changes therefore means running pi in a real PTY and streaming terminal bytes, or monkey-patching/embedding private internals.

RPC mode has a useful extension UI sub-protocol for select/confirm/input/editor/notify/status/widget/title/editor text, but it explicitly degrades TUI APIs: `custom()` returns undefined and working indicator/footer/header/editor/tools-expanded/theme APIs are no-op or unavailable. A semantic RPC mobile UI cannot honestly claim full community TUI extension compatibility.

Community TUI extensions can provide arbitrary Component render/handleInput logic, overlays, custom editors, custom footer/header/status/widgets, and custom message/tool renderers. Preserving these requires either rendering pi's TUI component tree itself or preserving a terminal/PTY boundary; simple chat/message rendering misses important APIs.
AgentSessionRuntime is the correct SDK layer for new/resume/fork/switch flows. Apps that replace sessions must re-subscribe and re-bind extensions after runtime.session changes.

Agentuity's remote-tui is the most relevant prior art for TUI fidelity without running the agent locally: it creates a local AgentSessionRuntime + InteractiveMode, monkey-patches prompt/steer/followUp/abort to send remote RPC commands, mirrors remote AgentSession events into the local session, handles hydration/replay/dedup/mid-stream attach, and lets native InteractiveMode render. This preserves local/native Pi TUI rendering better than a chat-only RPC UI, but still relies on internal/private state and must translate all remote events accurately.

@woxqaq/pi-web advertises a browser TUI-like experience and is packaged as a pi extension launched by `/web`, but the bridge uses SDK/WebSocket/session abstractions and a headless UI context where TUI-specific methods are no-op. It is useful as a session/web UI reference, not proof that arbitrary TUI components can render in browser.

@agegr/pi-web provides a Next.js/SSE web UI for browsing pi JSONL sessions, streaming conversation, branch/fork navigation, model switching, tools, compaction, steering, and follow-up. It is a strong semantic pi session UI reference but does not preserve the native TUI/extension component surface.

BlackBelt pi-agent-dashboard is mobile-friendly and mature for remote control: bridge extension + server + React client, active session mirroring, prompt routing/PromptBus for dialogs, session spawning headless or tmux, auth/tunnel options, and integrated xterm.js/node-pty terminal manager. It uses RPC/headless and custom browser UI for most session UX, so it improves mobile operations but does not fully reuse arbitrary pi TUI extensions.

Agent of Empires supports Pi.dev among many agents by managing real tmux sessions, exposing a web dashboard/PWA and remote phone access via Tailscale Funnel or Cloudflare Tunnel. Its value is orchestration, persistence, worktrees, and PTY terminal rendering in the web dashboard rather than Pi-specific extension compatibility.

pi-tui-web claims complete web TUI rendering but its architecture runs `pi --mode rpc`, maps 30+ RPC commands, and implements the RPC Extension UI protocol in browser. Because RPC's own docs say `ctx.ui.custom` and other TUI-specific methods are unavailable, this approach can mimic the standard TUI but cannot preserve arbitrary community TUI components.

OpenAI codex-app-server is a rich JSON-RPC app protocol over stdio JSONL, experimental WebSocket, Unix socket, or off. It exposes first-class thread/start/resume/fork/list/read, turn/start/steer/interrupt, typed item notifications, approvals, sandbox/permission knobs, file/process APIs, and backpressure/health behavior. It is a strong protocol reference but Codex-specific and not a Pi TUI-preserving solution.

Remodex is a native iOS + local bridge for Codex: a paired encrypted WebSocket session to a Mac bridge, which spawns or connects to `codex app-server` and forwards JSON-RPC while intercepting git/workspace/desktop/notification requests. It emphasizes local runtime, E2EE pairing, trusted reconnect, push, git actions, photos, and shared Codex thread history; it is not a terminal/TUI-preserving app.

Happy is an open-source mobile/web client for Claude Code and Codex. It wraps agents with `happy`, registers machines/daemon sessions, uses a Socket.IO relay with user/session/machine scopes and encrypted blobs, supports machine RPC for spawning/resuming sessions on configured machines, and uses a unified flat session-event protocol for mobile rendering. It is a semantic client/daemon architecture rather than a PTY/TUI-preserving renderer.

Happy Claude mode alternates between local and remote launchers. In local mode, it runs Claude normally, scans Claude JSONL files, and switches to remote mode when mobile sends a message/abort/switch; in remote mode it uses Claude SDK streaming and an Ink display, with 'press any key/double space' style local handoff. This is device-handoff UX, not TUI byte mirroring.

Happy Codex support hand-rolls a Codex app-server JSON-RPC client because the Codex SDK lacks app-server/approval callbacks, maps Codex events into Happy's session protocol, routes approval requests through mobile permission handlers, and lets mobile override permission mode/model/reasoning per message.

Happy's public docs describe a three-part CLI/mobile/relay architecture: the CLI runs on the user's computer, watches Claude Code, encrypts data, sends encrypted blobs to a relay, and the mobile app decrypts/renders. The docs explicitly say all display code lives in the mobile app and contrast Happy with raw terminal apps; this confirms it is not a TUI-preserving terminal relay.

The pi-mobile repository currently contains only `.pi/worklogs/...` and no committed project files, so the research output should create a new report document and commit it with the structured worklog.

content: Re-read and consolidated community project findings. Relevant pi-specific/community references include @woxqaq/pi-web, @agegr/pi-web, BlackBelt pi-agent-dashboard, Dwsy pi-tui-web, Agentuity coder remote-tui, pi-acp, AoE, OpenClaw, and smaller ports. The key split is semantic RPC/session UIs vs PTY/remote-native rendering; Agentuity remote-tui is the strongest TUI-fidelity reference.

Community search is complete enough for synthesis. No existing project found that is both Pi-specific, mobile-host oriented, and fully arbitrary TUI-extension preserving; the closest fidelity work is either PTY/tmux terminal access or Agentuity's native remote InteractiveMode mirror.
Starting codex app-server inspection recovery after context compaction.

Codex app-server review complete. It is an excellent mobile protocol reference (threads/turns/items, typed streaming notifications, approvals, sandbox/permissions, process/file utilities, resume/fork/list, backpressure), but it is Codex-specific and not a mechanism for preserving Pi's terminal TUI or community TUI extensions.
Starting Remodex inspection recovery after context compaction.

Remodex review complete. The architecture to borrow is local-first bridge + paired encrypted mobile session + optional relay + trusted reconnect + background daemon + git/workspace/notifications/attachments. It uses Codex app-server semantic JSON-RPC and mobile-native rendering, not PTY/TUI reuse.
Starting Happy/happy.engineering inspection recovery after context compaction, including public docs and source clone.

Happy review complete. Despite public copy such as 'every Claude Code feature works on mobile', the implementation is not a TUI wrapper: the CLI/mobile/relay design encrypts semantic session events, the app owns display rendering, machine RPC spawns/resumes configured hosts, and Claude/Codex adapters map provider output to a unified mobile protocol. Useful ideas: configured machines, daemon lifecycle, encrypted relay, offline/reconnect, push notifications, and local/remote handoff.

Starting synthesis/report writing. No blockers remain after the Happy/Remodex/Codex/community review; the remaining work is to document options, tradeoffs, and a recommended direct path for a Pi mobile client.
